title: Cost of Living in Toronto, Vancouver and Calgary: Student Housing and Budgeting

runs.t: The cost of living in Canada varies substantially by city, neighbourhood, housing type and lifestyle. Toronto and Vancouver are usually among the more expensive rental markets, while Calgary can offer lower asking rents for comparable accommodation. However, the cheapest rent is not always the lowest total cost: transport, distance to campus, utilities and the availability of student housing also matter.

Compare current room or apartment rents near the actual campus, then add utilities, food, transport, phone, insurance and personal expenses. IRCC’s living-expense amount is a study-permit financial benchmark, not a city-specific budget or a guarantee that the money will cover a student’s real costs.

sections.title: IRCC financial benchmark vs real living costs

runs.t: For study permit applications submitted on or after 1 September 2026, a single applicant studying outside Quebec must show CAD 23,448 for one year of living expenses, excluding tuition and transportation. This is a minimum immigration financial-capacity figure. Students should prepare a realistic budget for the city and housing they will actually use.

Statistics Canada publishes asking-rent estimates based on rental listings. These are not the same as average rents paid by existing tenants, university residence prices or a guaranteed quote for a particular neighbourhood. For the second quarter of 2026, the published average asking rent for a two-bedroom apartment was CAD 2,650 in Toronto, CAD 3,030 in Vancouver and CAD 1,890 in Calgary.

rows.t: Use a current room or residence quote near campus; include deposit and possible utilities.
Check whether heat, water, electricity and internet are included in rent.
Build a weekly grocery plan and include occasional meals outside.
Check the city transit pass, student concession and whether a campus U-Pass is included in fees.
Compare prepaid and monthly plans; include tax.
Use the programme’s list and distinguish one-time from recurring costs.
Check provincial health coverage rules, institution insurance and uncovered expenses.
Keep a separate reserve for deposits, winter clothing, travel and unexpected costs.

sections.title: Housing search: reduce cost and avoid scams

runs.t: Start with the university’s residence office and official off-campus housing resources.
Check the commute to the exact campus, not just the city centre. A cheaper room can create high transport costs.
Confirm whether the rent includes utilities, internet, furniture, laundry and parking.
Do not send deposits before verifying the property, landlord or authorised agent and the tenancy terms.
Be cautious of pressure to pay immediately, unusually low rents, requests for gift cards or refusal to arrange a viewing.
Read the province’s tenancy rules and understand the deposit limits, lease term and notice requirements.
Keep copies of the listing, lease, payment receipts and communications.

sections.title: The housing crisis is local, not identical across Canada

runs.t: Avoid describing every Canadian city as having the same “housing crisis”. Vacancy rates, new supply, student demand and rental prices vary by market and neighbourhood. The Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC) and Statistics Canada provide useful market-level context, but students still need campus-level research. A city average cannot predict the availability of a room when a particular intake begins.

faq.q: Is Toronto more expensive than Calgary for students?

runs.t: Rental asking-rent data for Q2 2026 shows higher two-bedroom asking rents in Toronto than Calgary. Total cost still depends on campus location, sharing, transport and lifestyle.

faq.q: Is Vancouver the most expensive city in Canada?

runs.t: It is among the most expensive major rental markets. Avoid a universal ranking without defining the city set, housing type and data period.

faq.q: Is CAD 23,448 enough to live in Canada for a year?

runs.t: It is IRCC’s minimum living-expense financial benchmark for one applicant outside Quebec from 1 September 2026. Actual costs may be higher, particularly for private housing in expensive markets.

faq.q: Should I book accommodation before my visa is approved?

runs.t: Students should understand cancellation terms and avoid non-refundable commitments they cannot afford to lose. Use verified university and housing resources.

faq.q: Can I work part-time to pay my rent?

runs.t: Eligible students may work off campus up to 24 hours per week during regular academic sessions and unlimited hours during scheduled breaks. Do not rely on future earnings to satisfy the study permit proof-of-funds requirement.
